events.title: Lebt und arbeitet in Wien
events.when: Last chance: closes Oct 26 · free entry Sun Oct 25, 10:00–18:00
events.description: “Lives and works in Vienna”: over 130 works by 56 artists based in the city, the Kunsthalle’s largest show of Viennese contemporary art in more than a decade. At MuseumsQuartier and Karlsplatz.
events.why: Last chance, and the Sunday before closing is free: a quick read on who makes art in Vienna now.

events.title: Tolia Astakhishvili: Figure of the Child
events.description: Solo show by the Georgian artist Tolia Astakhishvili at mumok, the museum of modern art in the MuseumsQuartier.
events.why: Last chance for one of the first shows of mumok’s new era under director Fatima Hellberg.

events.title: Terminal Piece
events.description: New mumok director Fatima Hellberg’s exhibition in five acts, built around the installation of the same name by the American artist and writer Kate Millett.
events.why: The opening statement of a new director at Vienna’s main modern art museum.

events.title: Women of the Wiener Werkstätte
events.description: The women designers of the Wiener Werkstätte, the Viennese design workshop founded in 1903. A cooperation with the Jewish Museum, New York.
events.why: Last chance for a show on the designers the Werkstätte story usually leaves out, at the museum that holds its archive.

events.title: Herbert Boeckl – Hans Josephsohn: Figural Archetypes
events.description: First joint show of the Austrian painter Herbert Boeckl and the Swiss sculptor Hans Josephsohn, two modernists of the human figure.
events.why: Pair it with the Leopold’s permanent Schiele and Vienna 1900 rooms in the same building.

events.title: Bernhard Leitner: SOUNDSPACESCULPTURE
events.when: Until Nov 22 · with Lap-See Lam and JJJJJerome Ellis
events.description: The Viennese sound artist Bernhard Leitner, who treats sound as a building material for space, at the Secession; shown alongside Lap-See Lam and JJJJJerome Ellis.
events.why: You can see Klimt’s Beethoven Frieze in the basement on the same ticket.

events.title: Erika Giovanna Klien: All Is Movement
events.description: Solo show for the artist and teacher at the heart of Viennese Kineticism, the 1920s movement, covering her work beyond the early kinetic pieces.
events.why: Vienna’s own 1920s avant-garde, a counterpoint to the Klimts across the garden in the Upper Belvedere.

events.title: Chudahye Chagis
events.description: Korean band built around Chu Da-hye, a sorikkun (traditional Korean singer), mixing shamanic song with psychedelic funk. Earlier, at 19:00: double bassist Luca Weigl solo.
events.why: Porgy & Bess is Vienna’s main jazz club, and its programming runs well beyond jazz; this is a typical night.

events.title: Fink
events.description: British singer-songwriter Fin Greenall’s band Fink on its European tour, in the big hall of Arena Wien.
events.why: Arena, in a former slaughterhouse in the 3rd district, is Vienna’s best-known independent rock venue.

events.title: Der fliegende Holländer
events.description: Wagner’s The Flying Dutchman, his first mature opera, about a sea captain cursed to sail until he finds a faithful wife.
events.why: Wagner in a house built in 1801, where Beethoven’s Fidelio had its premiere; far more intimate than the Staatsoper.

events.title: Nijinsky
events.description: John Neumeier’s ballet on the life of Vaslav Nijinsky, star of the Ballets Russes, to Chopin, Schumann, Rimsky-Korsakov and Shostakovich. New production for the Vienna State Ballet.
events.why: A premiere at the State Opera; the opening night is also livestreamed if you can’t get a seat.

events.title: Am Ziel
events.description: Thomas Bernhard’s play about a mother and daughter’s seaside summer, by Austria’s great literary scold, at the Burgtheater’s smaller house.
events.why: Bernhard on a Viennese stage is about as local as theatre gets; worth it if your German is good.

events.title: Hercules
events.description: Handel’s Hercules, a musical drama about the hero’s jealous wife Dejanira and the poisoned robe that kills him.
events.why: A single Handel evening at Theater an der Wien, which has made baroque opera one of its specialities.

events.title: Viennale
events.description: Vienna’s international film festival: new features and shorts, a Robert Aldrich retrospective, talks, and parties at the Viennale Zentrale in the old Funkhaus.
events.why: The city’s big cultural fortnight. For sold-out screenings, check the festival’s rest-ticket page.

events.title: Heat
events.description: Michael Mann’s 1995 Los Angeles heist film with Al Pacino and Robert De Niro, shown from the Film Museum’s own collection.
events.why: The Film Museum’s black-box cinema under the Albertina is one of the best places in Europe to see a film.

events.title: Robert Aldrich retrospective
events.when: Kiss Me Deadly Oct 23, 18:30 · Christian Petzold intro Oct 24
events.description: The Viennale’s retrospective of the Hollywood rebel behind Kiss Me Deadly, Baby Jane and The Dirty Dozen, mostly introduced by curator Christoph Huber; Dominik Graf introduces Nov 13–14.
events.why: Nearly every screening has a live introduction, and the run continues for two weeks after the festival ends.

events.title: Vienna 1900: guided tour in English
events.description: English-language tour of “Vienna 1900—Everyday. A Total Work of Art”, the MAK’s reinstalled collection of Wiener Werkstätte furniture, glass and design.
events.why: A guided way into Viennese modernism at the museum that holds the best of its applied arts.

events.title: Das Ferienhaus
events.description: Australian-Swiss director Simon Stone’s rewrite of Ibsen, on the Burgtheater’s main stage.
events.why: One of the few Burgtheater evenings offered with the PROMPT surtitle app on your phone.

events.title: L’Orfeo
events.description: Monteverdi’s 1607 Orpheus, one of the first operas, with Rolando Villazón and Nadezhda Karyazina; Stefan Gottfried conducts.
events.why: A chance to hear where opera began, in one of its grandest houses; four dates in the window.

events.title: Nationalfeiertag
events.description: Austria’s national holiday. The army usually puts on displays on Heldenplatz, and emergency services show their work at the Wiener Sicherheitsfest on Rathausplatz.
events.why: The day Viennese families wander the Ring looking at tanks and fire engines; a public holiday, so plan around closures.

events.title: Otello
events.description: Verdi’s Otello with Jonas Kaufmann in the title role, Nicole Car as Desdemona and Luca Salsi as Iago.
events.why: Kaufmann is listed for all five performances; book early.

events.title: Wir sind noch einmal davongekommen
events.description: Thornton Wilder’s The Skin of Our Teeth, his comedy of a family surviving the ice age, the flood and war, in German at the Burgtheater.
events.why: A play many English speakers know, with phone surtitles via the PROMPT app.

events.title: Wien Modern
events.description: Austria’s biggest festival of contemporary music, founded in 1988 at the initiative of Claudio Abbado, with a month of events across the city.
events.why: The other side of musical Vienna: new work, often in unusual spaces, played by top orchestras and ensembles.

events.title: Die letzten Tage der Menschheit
events.description: Karl Kraus’s vast satire of Vienna in the First World War, “The Last Days of Mankind”, once thought unstageable.
events.why: Kraus is Vienna’s sharpest critic of itself; surtitles and €25 anniversary tickets make it reachable.

events.title: Talk with Volker Schlöndorff
events.description: The German director of The Tin Drum, which won the Palme d’Or and an Oscar, in conversation at the Viennale’s festival centre in the old radio house.
events.why: A chance to hear a key figure of New German Cinema in person.

events.title: La Fille du régiment
events.description: Donizetti’s comedy in Laurent Pelly’s production, with Erin Morley and Xabier Anduaga; Evelino Pidò conducts.
events.why: Comic relief after the Verdi and Monteverdi; the tenor’s aria “Ah! mes amis” has nine high Cs.

events.title: Vienna Art Week
events.description: A week of tours, talks, open studios and exhibitions with around 70 museums, galleries and art schools. This year’s theme is “Navigating Angst”.
events.why: Free entry, and the open studio days get you into artists’ workspaces you couldn’t otherwise visit.

events.title: Imperial Lights
events.description: A garden of lights with baroque elements in the Schönbrunn Palace park.
events.why: Pairs with the palace Christmas market on the same evening.

events.title: Christmas Market at Schönbrunn Palace
events.description: Christmas market in the forecourt of the Habsburg summer palace, one of the first in the city to open.
events.why: Open before most markets, so you get the mulled wine and the palace backdrop without the December crowds.

events.title: Blickfang
events.description: Design sales fair with around 160 jury-selected exhibitors: furniture, lighting, fashion, jewellery and accessories, with the designers on hand.
events.why: Buy straight from Viennese and European designers, inside the city’s museum of applied arts.

events.title: Art&Antique
events.description: Art and antiques fair with Austrian and international dealers and galleries, from antiquity to contemporary design, in the imperial palace.
events.why: Browse Biedermeier and Jugendstil pieces in the Hofburg’s state halls, whether or not you buy.

events.title: Paper Positions Vienna
events.description: Art fair devoted to works on paper: drawings, collages and conceptual pieces from classical modernism to now, shown salon-style without booths.
events.why: A focused fair, smaller than Art&Antique and running the same weekend.

events.title: Simon Keenlyside recital
events.description: The English baritone Simon Keenlyside in a song recital on the main stage with pianist Malcolm Martineau.
events.why: A Lieder evening in the opera house itself, part of its “Grand Voices” series.

events.title: Viennese Christmas Market at Rathausplatz
events.description: The city’s biggest Christmas market, in front of the neo-Gothic City Hall, with the Vienna Ice World skating paths through the park.
events.why: Opening week, before the Christmas coach tours arrive.

events.title: Christmas Market at Spittelberg
events.description: Stalls along the narrow Biedermeier lanes of Spittelberg in the 7th district, with crafts and many local, fair-trade and organic products.
events.why: Small streets and crafts rather than souvenirs; quieter on weekday afternoons.

events.title: Kunst & Design Markt
events.description: Market for small designers, artists and producers selling fashion, jewellery, furnishings, chocolate and more, held in the Ottakringer brewery.
events.why: Early Christmas shopping from local makers, in one of Vienna’s last big working breweries.

events.title: Old Viennese Christmas Market
events.description: A market has been held on the Freyung since 1772; this one keeps to handicrafts, glass decorations, nativity figures and ceramics.
events.why: The traditional option in the old town, with live Advent music in the afternoons.
